event_config: Benchmark campaign at FIXED epsilon = 2 mrad (EPS_FIXED = 0.002), filter is exact: (eps_provenance == 'set') & (epsilon.round(6) == 0.002) — NOT the Efficiency Frontier formula-epsilon. Noise triple confirmed in metrics.csv slice: sigma_scatt = 1e-4, sigma_res = 0.0, hit_ineff (hit drop) in {0.0, 0.01}. gamma in {1, 2, 3}, delta = 1, kernel = 'step' only, phi_max = 0.2. Solvers present in the slice (2036 rows): classical 1230, qsvt 506, quantum 300. T grid (n_trk): {10, 20, 30, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 550, 700, 1000}. Reps per (solver, gamma, hit_ineff, n_trk) cell BEFORE the gate: classical 20 at n_trk in {10,20,50,100,200,400,700,1000}, 10 at {30,75,150,300}, 5 at 550 (distinct reps 0-19 verified, no duplicates); quantum 3-10 (0 at some gamma in {1,2} hit_ineff=0.01 cells for n_trk in {30,75,150,300,550}); qsvt 3-10, 5 at n_trk >= 550 for gamma=3. Validity gate: add_validity, valid = classical-partner max|x| <= EXPLODE_MAX = 50.0 (same event_key+ham_key; quantum/qsvt judged by the partner because rescaling hides the explosion; no partner => invalid); drops 121/2036 rows, 19.3% at gamma=1, 0.3% at gamma=2, 0% at gamma=3 — docstring records the ungated bias as 7.4pp at n_trk=200.
per_curve_conventions: Each agg_by_ntrk call yields ONE solver's curves (caller picks solver in {classical, quantum, qsvt} x gamma x hit_ineff), and every curve carries TWO working-point conventions side by side: (1) fixed gamma-aware absolute tau = delta/(delta+gamma) + 0.10 (qp.threshold_for; = 0.35 at gamma=3, 0.433 at gamma=2, 0.60 at gamma=1) -> se_m/se_e, fr_m/fr_e, tam/fam — kept as the DIAGNOSTIC comparison; (2) wp99 efficiency-first per-solve threshold (columns *_wp; tau set just below the 1% quantile of TRUE-segment amplitudes so >= 99% of true segments survive, WP_TARGET_EFF = 0.99, floored at WP_TAU_FLOOR = 1e-6 to honestly report 1BQF structural zeroing of isolated clusters) -> se_wp_m/fr_wp_m/tam_wp/fam_wp — the HEADLINE working point per build_metrics.py >= 2026-06-14. Quantum/qsvt amplitudes are first rescaled to the classical SIGNAL support (rescale_to_signal: match L2 norm on sol_C > tau; NOT full ||sol_C||, which is false-bulk dominated), then thresholded; segment_false_rate = n_false_active / n_active (= 1 - purity), not the leakage rate.
aggregation: Per-n_trk mean +/- SEM (std ddof=1 / sqrt(n)) over valid reps, per (solver, gamma, hit_ineff) slice; n_reps reported as the MINIMUM group size across the n_trk grid. _sem returns 0.0 for single-rep cells, so error bars silently vanish where the gamma=1 gate leaves 1 rep.
red_flags: No cross-campaign mixing: the exact eps_provenance=='set' & epsilon==0.002 filter cleanly isolates the fixed-2 mrad benchmark from the Efficiency Frontier formula-epsilon campaign, and the module docstring labels this. Residual cautions: (1) agg_by_ntrk returns fixed-tau and wp99 arrays in one dict, so any figure drawn from it must state which convention each curve uses — the convention choice lives in the (unaudited-here) notebook, not the data layer; (2) rep counts are heterogeneous across the n_trk grid (5-20 classical, 0-10 quantum/qsvt; several quantum gamma in {1,2}, hit_ineff=0.01 cells are empty at n_trk in {30,75,150,300,550}), and the single n_reps=min value understates most points while SEM=0 masks 1-rep gamma=1 cells after the ~19% validity drop; (3) the raw-vector path (solves_index/load_vectors) applies NO validity gate — exploded lambda_min->0 solves pass through to amplitude/spectrum notebooks unless the caller gates them; (4) at gamma=1 hit_ineff cells the post-gate survivors are a biased subset (up to ~100% of high-T cells explode per the docstring), so gamma=1 curves at high n_trk rest on very few events.
